Now I have enough information to provide a complete explanation. Let me trace through the complete lifecycle one more time to make sure I have it right.

The membership invitation lifecycle in this Taskflow application follows this flow:

## 1. Invitation Creation (Admin Action)

When an admin types a colleague's email into the members settings page, the `inviteMemberForm.tsx` component handles the submission. The form:
- Validates the email against `inviteMemberSchema` (checking format and basic constraints)
- Checks `can()` permission to ensure the actor has `member:invite` capability
- Verifies the seat quota via `getPlanLimits()` to ensure accepting would not exceed the plan's seat limit

This validation happens twice: once client-side in `invite-member-form.tsx` (lines 50, 54) and again server-side in the action.

## 2. Server-Side Action Processing

The `inviteMemberAction` in `src/actions/members/invite-member.ts` runs with authorization checks:
- Uses `withAction()` wrapper to enforce schema validation
- Calls `can()` to verify `member:invite` permission on the organization
- Calls `consumeRateLimit()` to enforce the invite rate limit (using the `member:invite` bucket, one quota per invite)
- Queries `getOrganizationSummary()` to get current seat usage
- Calls `inviteMember()` service function

## 3. Invitation Service Logic

The `inviteMember()` function in `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` (line 28) performs the core work:
- Calls `assertOrgScope()` and `assertCan()` to re-verify permissions
- Calls `consumeRateLimit()` with the `member:invite` bucket (one charge per person)
- Fetches the organization to validate it exists
- Counts both `countActiveMembers()` and `countPendingInvitations()` against the seat quota using `wouldExceedLimit()` — pending invitations hold seats
- For each invite, generates a 32-byte random token via `randomToken()`, hashes it with `hashToken()`, and passes only the hash to the repository

## 4. Database Storage

The `invitationRepo.insertInvitation()` function in `src/server/repositories/invitation-repository.ts` (line 16) stores:
- `id`: a unique identifier
- `orgId`: tenant scope
- `email`: the invitee's email address
- `role`: the role being granted (e.g., "member", "admin")
- `invitedBy`: the ID of the admin who sent the invite
- `tokenHash`: the bcrypt-style hash of the token (the plain token is never stored)
- `expiresAt`: calculated as 14 days from now by default
- `acceptedAt`, `revokedAt`: both null initially
- `createdAt`, `updatedAt`: timestamps

The database uses a unique index on `tokenHash` (so each token can only be redeemed once) and an index on `(orgId, email)` (to prevent duplicate invites to the same email).

## 5. Event Emission

Once the invitation row is created, `invitationService` emits a `member.invited` event (line 101) containing:
- `orgId`
- `actorId`: the inviter's user ID
- `occurredAt`: the invitation creation timestamp
- `email`: the invitee's address
- `role`: the granted role

This event is published to the event bus (`emit()` in `src/lib/event-bus.ts`), where it triggers any subscribed handlers. Currently no handlers subscribe to `member.invited` directly — this may be where email sending would be wired in the future.

## 6. What Travels in the Link

The plain token is never returned to the client or sent in an email in the current codebase. The `toInvitation()` mapper in `src/server/repositories/_mappers.ts` (line 165) returns the stored `tokenHash` under the key `token` to the client, which means the hashed value is what would be visible in the UI. However, the actual invitation link pattern would require the plain token to be sent to the email address — the route `/invite/[token]/page.tsx` expects a token parameter that gets validated with `invitationTokenSchema` (checking it's 32–128 characters and alphanumeric/dash/underscore).

## 7. Link Acceptance

When the invitee clicks the link (at `/invite/[token]`), the `page.tsx` route (line 21) runs with `dynamic: "force-dynamic"` to ensure no caching:
- Validates the token format using `invitationTokenSchema`
- If the visitor is not signed in, redirects to `/login?next=/invite/[token]`
- If signed in, renders the `InviteAcceptForm`, which shows the accept button

## 8. Acceptance Action

When the accept button is clicked, `acceptInvitationAction()` in `src/actions/members/accept-invitation.ts` runs:
- Parses the token from form data with `acceptInvitationTokenSchema`
- Gets the current session principal (requires the user to be signed in)
- Calls `acceptInvitation()` service function, passing the user's ID and the token

## 9. Invitation Validation

The `acceptInvitation()` service function (line 117 of invitation-service.ts) performs several checks:
- `findInvitationByTokenHash()`: looks up the invitation using the hashed token as the key
- Checks `revokedAt !== null` — refuses if revoked
- Checks `acceptedAt !== null` — refuses if already accepted
- Compares `expiresAt` against the current time — refuses if expired
- Checks if the user is already a member of that organization (returns existing membership if so)

## 10. Membership Creation & Event Emission

Once all checks pass, `invitationService.acceptInvitation()` calls:
- `memberRepo.insertMember()` to create the membership row with:
  - `userId`: the accepting user
  - `orgId`: from the invitation
  - `role`: from the invitation
  - `invitedBy`: preserved from the invitation
  - `status`: set to "active"
  - `joinedAt`: current timestamp
- `invitationRepo.markInvitationAccepted()` to set the `acceptedAt` timestamp on the invitation row
- `emit("member.joined", ...)` with the new member's details

The `member.joined` event triggers the `notification-service.ts` subscriber (line 231), which calls `notify()` to send an in-app notification to the organization's owner that a new member joined.

## 11. Final Seat Quota Check

Back in `acceptInvitationAction()` (line 38), the action calls `assertSeatAvailable()` to re-check the plan quota after the membership has been created, in case other invitations were accepted between the time the link was sent and this moment. If seats have since filled up, the membership is rolled back by the error.

The user is then redirected to either `/orgs` (if no org slug in the link params) or to the organization's home page, entering the workspace as a full member.
